approach: Add run/ci.rs holding the CI branch push, the CI-backed source and the delete. After the candidate is admitted (start of `check_and_verify`, once the disk gate has passed, unless the checks are resumed), push the candidate with athena-git to `athena/ci/<job id>`, only when `origin` is an https github.com URL and the run is not nested. Keep the push in a `RefCell` on `RunContext`. In the checks stage, build the source for that branch (`GhClient::ci_source`) and call a new `routing::run_routed_recorded` (`run_routed` plus the CI record it used). Pass `resolve` a `Wait` derived from the new `[budget] ci_wait_s` (default 1500). Without a push, `NoCi` stands in inside ci.rs, so nothing changes and `run/mod.rs` no longer passes it. When the record's source is CI, `verify::reuse_statement` goes to the verifier as one more `CheckResultView` entry, the way the report-gaps entry is passed. `dispatch` runs everything after the `RunContext` is built, and the branch is deleted once on every exit (Ok or Err). The reread path recurses before any push, so it never deletes. The remote and platform are injected through a `#[cfg(test)]` seam in ci.rs, next to the existing `check_seam` that counts local runs. ci.yml gets an `athena/ci/**` push trigger. Round-2 fix: the criterion 9 demonstration now names its seam (the full workspace test run, whose new tests drive `Athena::go` through `ci_seam` and `check_seam`) and what fails without the behavior (fmt, clippy -D warnings, or the new tests).

decisions.choice: A new trait `CiBranchRemote` (push, delete) in run/ci.rs, implemented over `athena_git::Git`, with a test-only seam `ci_seam` carrying `(Rc<dyn CiBranchRemote>, Rc<dyn CiSource>)`.
decisions.reason: Adding a delete method to `gh::Remote` would touch gh/remote.rs, test_support.rs and gh/tests.rs, none of them deliverables, and client.rs is out of scope. The seam sits in a deliverable file and follows the existing `early_seam` and `check_seam` pattern.

rejected.why: It needs edits to non-deliverable files (remote.rs, gh/mod.rs, test_support.rs).
It would change gh/client.rs, which is kept as landed.

decisions.choice: Delete in `dispatch`, around everything built after the `RunContext`, keyed on `ctx.ci_push` being set.
decisions.reason: One place for all close paths: accepted, failed, rejected, early stop and error. The reread recursion returns before the context exists, so the delete runs once.

rejected.why: It has several callers, and an `Err` from `produce_and_verify` skips it.
The delete needs `&Athena`, the seam and the ui, so a guard would hide it and swallow errors.

decisions.choice: Hand the verifier the reuse statement as an extra `CheckResultView` named `ci-result` (passed, `command` = "not a check", detail = `reuse_statement(record, sha)`), added in verification.rs.
decisions.reason: `VerifierInputs` lives in athena-context, outside the deliverables. The producer-report-gaps entry already uses this channel.

rejected.why: It changes the athena-context brief, prompt budgets and its tests.

decisions.choice: Add `routing::run_routed_recorded` returning the check runs and `Option<CiRecord>` (Some only when its source is CI); `run_routed` delegates and drops the record.
decisions.reason: Existing routing tests keep passing, and the CI record reaches the caller.

rejected.why: It breaks the callers and tests in routing.rs.

decisions.choice: `[budget] ci_wait_s` is a `#[serde(default = ...)] u64` (default 1500) in `Budget`, with 1500 in athena.toml. `Wait` = pause 20 s, polls = ceil(bound/20)+1; a bound of 0 gives one read.
decisions.reason: deny_unknown_fields plus no default would break every embedded test config. A zero bound lets the timed-out test run without sleeping.

rejected.why: It breaks every embedded config in the tests.
A second table for one number; `[budget]` already holds `check_timeout_s`.

decisions.choice: A push failure, a missing origin, a non-https or non-github origin or a nested run means no push, `NoCi`, and the existing local path. A push failure prints one warning line.
decisions.reason: Keeps the fallback rule and the 'no GitHub remote: nothing changes' rule; matches how `early_pr` skips.

rejected.option: Fail the job on push failure
rejected.why: CI reuse is an optimisation; the local checks still decide.

decisions.choice: Criterion 9 is demonstrated by the three Athena gate commands run over the whole workspace, with the new ci_tests as the behavior carried by `cargo test`.
decisions.reason: The criterion is a gate on the other changes: fmt catches unformatted new files, clippy -D warnings catches dead code left by the change (an unused `NoCi` import, an unused seam, unused helper), and cargo test runs the Athena::go tests that fail if any wired behavior is missing.

rejected.why: It would not exercise athena-git, athena-data, the xtask policy scan or the budget test, or fmt and clippy.

risks.risk: A job killed before close leaves `athena/ci/<job id>` on the remote.
risks.mitigation: The delete runs on every normal exit, including Err. A leftover is harmless: the name is reused only on a retry with the same id, and deleting a missing branch counts as success. No sweeper is added (out of scope); the CHANGELOG says so.

risks.risk: Adding `ci_wait_s` to athena.toml changes the config hash, so queued readings are read again once.
risks.mitigation: Known effect of any `[budget]` change; the reread path handles it; the CHANGELOG mentions it.

risks.risk: A 25-minute wait with 20 s polls makes real waits in a real run, and tests that wait would sleep.
risks.mitigation: Tests use `ci_wait_s = 0` (one read, no sleep) for the timeout case; green, red and missing replies return on the first poll; a pure test checks the Wait values for 0 and 1500.

risks.risk: A candidate that changes a workflow file pushes a branch whose push the token may refuse, or whose green run `resolve` ignores.
risks.mitigation: `resolve` already ignores a green run when a workflow file changed, and a refused push is a warning that falls back to the local checks.

risks.risk: The ci.yml cache saves only from the default branch, so the first runs on athena/ci/** are cold and may exceed the wait.
risks.mitigation: On timeout `resolve` falls back to the local checks: correct, only slower; the bound is a config value.

risks.risk: The same SHA already on the remote under another branch could give a run that is not the push run.
risks.mitigation: The source is built per branch by `GhClient::ci_source(branch)`, which reads only the push run of that branch (g437); the pull_request-only test shows it.

demonstrations.method: Run `Athena::go` on a fake-driver job in a temp repo with `origin` set to an https github.com URL. Inject a recording `CiBranchRemote` and a canned green push-run `CiSource` (it echoes the SHA it is asked about) through `ci_seam::install`; install `check_seam` with a counter. Assert zero local runs; the source was asked for exactly the SHA the remote was given to push, which is the candidate commit in the job's candidate record; the stored check records have notes naming CI and the run address; the committed brief-verifier.md contains the `reuse_statement` text.
demonstrations.observes: check_seam counter reads 0, the check records say the result was reused from the CI run for the SHA, and the verifier brief carries the statement.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `NoCi` or no `resolve` call the counter is 3 and the notes name a local source, so the assertions fail; without the reuse statement the brief assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `Athena::go` (exists). `ci_seam::install` and the `CiBranchRemote`/`CiSource` fakes are added in steps 3 and 10. `check_seam::install` exists in run/mod.rs (used in run/tests.rs). Origin is added with `athena.git.run(["remote","add","origin","https://github.com/example/project.git"])`; the real `Athena::github_repository` guard runs, the fakes only record and reply.

demonstrations.method: Same harness, one test per case: (a) a red run with a failing step named: outcome is failed or rejected, the reason names the failing check, counter 0. (b) no run, (c) cancelled run, (d) timed_out run, (e) unfinished run with `ci_wait_s = 0` (wait times out), (f) a run for a different SHA, (g) an Err from the source: each leaves the counter at 3 and the records name local runs. The pull_request-only case: build a client with `GhClient::ci_source(branch)` over an inline fake `gh::Runner` whose runs reply holds only a pull_request run and assert the fetch gives None, then the Athena::go fallback with a None source gives counter 3. Do not edit gh/tests.rs.
demonstrations.observes: Red test: counter 0 and a reason holding the check name. Every fallback test: counter 3.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the red path the red job runs the local checks (counter 3) or passes; without the fallback a missing, cancelled or timed-out run would block or error the job.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go`, `ci_seam` (step 3, fakes in step 10), `check_seam` (exists). Fake `Runner` is the existing `gh` runner trait; if it is private to `gh`, the pull_request-only case is covered by the Athena::go test with a None source plus the g437 reply-parsing tests already in gh/tests.rs.

demonstrations.method: Same harness with a `CiBranchRemote` that logs ('push', branch, commit) and ('delete', branch) in order, with a probe recording whether a candidate record exists when the push arrives. Run `go` to an accepted outcome, a failed outcome (red CI) and a rejected outcome (verifier fails): one push of `athena/ci/<job id>` of the candidate commit, then one delete of the same branch after the closing commit. Also an Err exit (forced disk hold or driver error after push) still deletes. Reread case: change an athena.toml setting that bears on a reading between the read and `go` with `AcceptedBy::Flag` so `dispatch` recurses; exactly one push and one delete.
demonstrations.observes: The call log is exactly [push, delete] on the same branch for each outcome, and one of each on the reread path.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no delete the log lacks the delete; with the delete in the wrong place the reread case shows two deletes or none; with the push before admission the probe sees no candidate record.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go`; recording `CiBranchRemote` injected through `ci_seam` (step 3, fake in step 10). Reread setup copied from the existing reread test (search run/tests.rs and run/pin.rs for 'reading again under the new configuration' and `reread_after_configuration_change`).

demonstrations.observes: Empty call log and 3 local check runs for each origin form.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the github remote guard were missing, the push and delete would appear in the log and the counter would be 0 or the source would be asked.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go`; the guard under test is the real `Athena::github_repository` (added in step 4, from `https_github_repository` in gh/early.rs); `ci_seam` fakes only record (step 3); `check_seam` exists.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gates Athena runs, one after the other, over the whole workspace. `cargo test --locked` includes the new `run::ci_tests` (Athena::go through the injected CI branch remote, CI source and check counter), the athena-git delete test, the athena-data config tests, the routing unit test, and the xtask policy and budget tests that scan the new text. Each command must exit 0.
demonstrations.command:
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0; the test summary shows the new ci_tests passing and no test failed or ignored by the change.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without formatting the new files, `cargo fmt --check` exits non-zero. With dead code left by the change (an unused `NoCi` import, an unused seam or helper) or any warning, clippy -D warnings exits non-zero. If the push, the `resolve` call, the delete, the fallback or the config default were missing or wrong, the ci_tests or config tests fail, and so does `cargo test`; a new text in the docs or code that breaks the boundary scan or the system-facts budget fails the xtask/budget tests.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points are the cargo commands over the workspace. The behavior inside `cargo test` is driven through `Athena::go` with the `ci_seam` fakes (added in steps 3 and 10) and the existing `check_seam` counter (exists in run/mod.rs); nothing is a double of the logic under test, the fakes only record calls and return canned runs.

open_questions: Does `judge` name the failing check in the final-verdict reasons for a failed (not pre-existing) check? The red-run test needs the name in the job reason; verify.rs is touched only if it does not.
Does the candidate commit exist in `self.git`'s object store when `check_and_verify` starts? `early_pr` pushes the same commit, so it should; the producer checks it against the test fixture.

Which existing test drives the reread path with `AcceptedBy::Flag`? A text search of run/tests.rs did not find one; the producer may need to build one by changing a reading-relevant setting in athena.toml.
The reuse statement is passed as a check entry because `VerifierInputs` is in athena-context (not a deliverable); is that acceptable, or should the brief type gain a field?
Whether the `gh::Runner` trait is visible outside `gh`, for the pull_request-only fetch test in ci_tests.rs.
